response.answer: Label uncertainty can be quantified using probabilistic labels or label smoothing, and it improves model robustness and calibration. Label smoothing reduces overconfidence by distributing label probabilities more evenly. Calibration ensures accurate downstream decision thresholds.

results.title: Label Smoothing: ML Regularization | Ultralytics
results.content: Enhance AI model accuracy and robustness with label smoothing—a proven technique to improve generalization and reduce overconfidence. ## Train Ultralytics YOLO models to streamline workflows across industries. ## Train AI models in seconds with Ultralytics YOLO. Label smoothing is a regularization technique used during the training of machine learning models to prevent the neural network from becoming overly confident in its predictions. By slightly modifying the target labels, this method encourages the model to produce less extreme probability distributions, which ultimately leads to better generalization and improved performance on unseen data. It effectively mitigates the common issue of overfitting, where a model memorizes the training data rather than learning the underlying patterns necessary for accurate predictions in real-world scenarios. In standard supervised learning tasks, such as image classification, models are typically trained using "hard" targets. ## Implementing Label Smoothing with Ultralytics. When using the Ultralytics YOLO11 model, you can enable label smoothing directly within the training arguments. The following example demonstrates how to train a model with label smoothing applied:. from ultralytics import YOLO # Load the YOLO11 classification model model = YOLO("yolo11n-cls.pt") # Train on a dataset with label smoothing set to 0.1 # This distributes 10% of the probability mass to incorrect classes model.train(data="mnist", epochs=5, label_smoothing=0.1). One of the primary advantages of label smoothing is the improvement of model calibration. Hard labels often lead to uncalibrated models that predict with 99% confidence regardless of the actual uncertainty. Label smoothing helps medical image analysis models avoid making dangerously confident false-positive predictions, assisting radiologists by providing more nuanced probability scores rather than binary certainties. Label smoothing acknowledges this ambiguity by preventing the model from assigning zero probability to valid synonyms, a concept crucial in Transformers and Large Language Models. It is helpful to distinguish label smoothing from other techniques used to improve model performance. Unlike label smoothing, where the soft targets are uniform and heuristic, distillation uses learned probabilities that contain information about the relationships between classes (e.g., a "dog" is more like a "cat" than a "car"). By integrating label smoothing into your training pipeline, you ensure that your models remain adaptable and calibrated, which is essential for successful model deployment in production environments.

results.title: How label smoothing and label flipping increases the performance of a machine learning model - Data Science Stack Exchange
results.content: # How label smoothing and label flipping increases the performance of a machine learning model Modified 5 years, 3 months ago I have seen posts and research papers mentioning these techniques for improving the performance of a machine learning model. However, I am wondering if these two techniques are **proven** to be beneficial for a ML model in the case when the labelling is correct? edited Jan 26, 2020 at 11:42 29711 gold badge66 silver badges1313 bronze badges asked Jul 9, 2019 at 11:18 1,12733 gold badges1414 silver badges2929 bronze badges ## 2 Answers 2 Label flipping is a training technique where one selectively manipulates the labels in order to make the model more robust against label noise and associated attacks - the specifics depend a lot on the nature of the noise. Label smoothing is a regularization technique (and then some) aimed at improving model performance. From *1 Adversarial Perturbations of Deep Neural Networks*, 2016: > Without label smoothing, a softmax classifier is trained to make infinitely confident predictions on the training set. When values are pushed outside the areas where training data concentrates, the model makes even more extreme predictions when extrapolating linearly. Label smoothing penalizes the model for making overly confident predictions on the training set, forcing it to learn either a more non-linear function or a linear function with smaller slope. Extrapolations by the label-smoothed model are consequently less extreme. As a result of label smoothing, the model becomes more robust in general. However, one cannot claim that the effects of label smoothing are purely beneficial. With label smoothing, the model is encouraged to treat each incorrect class as equally probable. answered Jul 31, 2019 at 8:19 62033 silver badges77 bronze badges Suppose you have a language model trained to predict the next word. Without label smoothing, you would be telling the network $$ P(\mathrm{you}|\textrm{hello},\textrm{how},\textrm{are}) = 1.0 $$ That is, "you" will always follow the three word "hello, how, are". results.content: Published Time: 2020-12-24T14:55:32+09:00 Loading [Contrib]/a11y/accessibility-menu.js Catch up on the latest AI articles * The Truth Behind Label Smoothing！ The Truth Behind Label Smoothing！ Deep Learning 04/01/2021 _**3 Main Points**_✔️ Relationship between label smoothing and loss-correction techniques ✔️ Effect of label smoothing on label noise ✔️Applications of label smoothing in knowledge distillation with noisy labels > Does label smoothing mitigate label noise? > written byMichal Lukasik,Srinadh Bhojanapalli,Aditya Krishna Menon,Sanjiv Kumar > (Submitted on 5 Mar 2020) > Subjects:Machine Learning (cs.LG); Machine Learning (stat.ML) To put it simply, label smoothing is the process of mixing a uniform vector to the available training labels and making them “softer”. It is a technique commonly employed while training neural networks in the presence of noisy labels. Neural networks can fit noisy labels easily. So it is natural to think that label smoothing tackles noisy labels by reducing overconfidence in a particular example. Nevertheless, it can also worsen the problem by injecting additional uniform noise to all the labels! Well then, does label smoothing really affect the robustness of deep networks?
